etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English chaungeable, from Old Northern French chaungeable, from Late Latin cambiāre (“to change”), equivalent to change +‎ -able.

definitions.definition: Subject to sudden or frequent changes.

quote.citation: 2021 October 20, Paul Stephen, “Leisure and Pleasure on the Far North Line”, in RAIL, number 942, page 48:
quote.text: There will be no problems with visibility, or the highly changeable Highland weather, as Scotland basks in what is reported to be the country's hottest September day for more than a century.

The weather is very changeable today: wind and rain in the same half-hour.

definitions.definition: (of a species) Capable of camouflaging itself by changing colour.
